market_view: Calm regime: VIX 15.6 and falling, 10-year yield 4.48%, dollar firm near 100.9. Chips are volatile after a big 60-day surge; oil is deeply sold off.

oil_gas.reasoning: WTI is down 26% in 20 days and XOM is down 10%, but the headlines hold nothing on OPEC+, supply or XOM. A driver move that already happened is priced in, so no named catalyst.

gold_miners.reasoning: Gold bounced 1% yesterday but is still down 7.5% over 20 days against a firm dollar and 4.5% yields. No NEM or gold headline. A one-day bounce is not a catalyst.

chips.reasoning: Only commentary headlines ('Nasdaq Weakness Shows AI Stocks Are Losing Their Easy Momentum', Investing.com; 'Flash Crash or Cash?', Investing.com), mostly about memory. Nothing specific to NVDA. TSMC sales around the 10th add variance only.

pharma.reasoning: Only a retail piece, 'Is It Too Late to Buy Eli Lilly Stock?' (Motley Fool), with no new fact. LLY is 2% from its high with no trial, regulatory or pricing news.

copper_uranium.reasoning: No copper or uranium supply or demand headline. Copper is 7% below its high and FCX is down 12% over 20 days, which is not a catalyst.

would_change_my_mind: A named company or commodity event: OPEC+ or supply news, a guidance raise or pre-announcement for XOM/NEM/NVDA/LLY/FCX, an export-rule change, or an FDA decision.

handoff.what_changed: WARNING: the previous note was for 2026-07-01 and its next job was 2026-07-02, so days 07-02 to 07-06 were not run here; I treated the note as stale-ish but held no positions. Headlines again held no qualifying catalyst for any leader, so all five families stay flat. Chips bounced (AMD +6.6%, TSM +4.1% on 07-06) and gold rose 1%.

oil_gas.why: WTI is down 26% in 20 days and no OPEC+ or XOM headline gives a one-sided setup.

gold_miners.why: Gold is weak against a firm dollar and yields, and no miner catalyst appears.

chips.why: Headlines are sector commentary on AI and memory, with nothing specific to NVDA.

pharma.why: No LLY-specific news; the stock is near its high.

copper_uranium.why: No copper or uranium supply or demand headline.
